data.title: Jyong Biotech Announces Receipt of Letter of Intent from a Philippine Enterprise to Explore Commercialization of Investigational Innovative Drug in the Philippines
data.description:
NEW TAIPEI CITY, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Jyong Biotech Ltd. (Nasdaq: MENS) (the "Company" or "Jyong Biotech"), a science-driven biotechnology company dedicated to the development and commercialization of innovative plant-derived therapeutics, today announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Health Ever Bio-Tech Co., Ltd., has entered into a Letter of Intent ("LOI") with a Philippine healthcare enterprise. The LOI initiates an evaluation of a potential collaboration for the in-licensing, development, and commercialization of Jyong Biotech's investigational new drug in the Philippines.

Aligning with the Company's strategy to expand patient access in Southeast Asia, the LOI expresses the Philippine enterprise's intent to evaluate the potential in-licensing and distribution of Botreso®, an investigational therapy for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Through this potential collaboration, the Philippine enterprise expects to explore the Philippine regulatory pathway, market opportunities, and commercialization strategies for Botreso®.

According to the Global Burden of Disease (GBD 2021) and BMC Urology research, the global BPH patient population reached 112.5 million in 2021, representing an increase of over 122% from 50.7 million in 1990, and is projected to grow to between 150 million and 156 million by 2035. Despite this market growth, a significant unmet medical need remains due to the severe side effects and high discontinuation rates of existing treatments. Current BPH treatments primarily rely on medications such as alpha-blockers and 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (5-ARIs). However, these drugs are associated with a five-year discontinuation rate of 60% to 90% due to adverse effects like dizziness, orthostatic hypotension, ejaculatory dysfunction, and sexual dysfunction.

As an innovative botanical therapy, Botreso® aims to address this clinical gap. The drug has conducted four Phase III clinical trials in the U.S. and Taiwan, becoming the first Taiwanese-developed oral botanical new drug to advance to Phase III clinical trials with the U.S. FDA. Botreso® is being developed as a potential well-tolerated treatment option suitable for long-term use.

"Receiving this LOI from a Philippine enterprise marks an important step in our strategy to evaluate new markets for Botreso® in Southeast Asia," said Fu-Feng Kuo, Chairwoman and Chief Executive Officer of Jyong Biotech." Their experience in the Philippine regulatory landscape and commercial network make them a promising potential partner. We look forward to evaluating this opportunity as we advance the global commercialization of our innovative BPH treatments."

Headquartered in Metro Manila, the potential partner is a Philippine healthcare solutions company with established expertise in pharmaceutical regulatory affairs, product registration, market access, and commercialization. Its experience working with international pharmaceutical and vaccine manufacturers and its relationships in the Philippine healthcare sector position it to support the potential introduction of Botreso® in the Philippines.

The LOI is non-binding, and there can be no assurance that any definitive agreement will be entered into. Any definitive agreement remains subject to due diligence, further evaluation of the product's clinical data, development status, regulatory requirements, and commercial terms. Moving forward, Jyong Biotech will continue leveraging its botanical platform to build a comprehensive BPH/LUTS portfolio centered on Botreso®, while accelerating the global development, out-licensing, and commercialization of its new drugs.

As of the date of this press release, Botreso® remains an investigational new drug candidate and has not been approved for commercial use in any jurisdiction.

About Jyong Biotech Ltd.

Headquartered in Taiwan, Jyong Biotech Ltd. is a science-driven biotechnology company committed to developing and commercializing innovative and differentiated new drugs (plant-derived), mainly specializing in the treatment of urinary system diseases, with an initial focus on the markets of the U.S., the EU and Asia. Since its inception in 2002, the Company has built integrated capabilities that encompass all key functionalities of drug development, including early-stage drug discovery and development, pharmacology, toxicology, clinical trials, regulatory affairs, manufacturing, and commercialization. Leveraging strong research and development capabilities and a proprietary platform, the Company has been developing a series of botanical drug candidates, including its primary botanical drug candidate, Botreso®, another clinical-stage botanical drug candidate, and other preclinical-stage botanical drug candidates. The Company endeavors to develop and supply first-class innovative drugs to meet customers' health needs and seeks to be a valuable business organization that is held in high esteem by the public. For more information, please visit: https://jyongir.com/.

data.title: NVDA Shorts Lose $12B As Huang’s Return Erases Nearly 90% Of Recent Gains, Says S3 Partners
data.description:
Key points:
  • Short sellers collected about $13.7 billion in mark-to-market gains in the seven days that NVDA shares fell after Huang’s exit, including $5.9 billion on Friday alone. 
  • Even after Monday’s losses, short sellers remain up about $4 billion on Nvidia for 2026.
  • Nasdaq shorts, meanwhile, incurred an estimated $39 billion loss on Monday, more than reversing Friday’s profit.

Short sellers betting against Nvidia (NVDA) lost roughly $12 billion in a single session on Monday after the company’s shares jumped over 30% after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO, according to S3 Partners.

According to the analytics firm, the one-day hit wiped out nearly 90% of the gains those same short positions had built over the previous seven trading days. NVDA stock closed up 31.5% on Monday after the company reinstated Huang as CEO, causing a broader rally in tech and AI names that pushed the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite index up 7%.

Seven Days Of Gains Vanish

After Huang stepped down following allegations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, Nvidia shares fell for seven straight sessions. Short sellers collected about $13.7 billion in mark-to-market gains during that stretch, including $5.9 billion on Friday alone when reports of the Securities and Exchange Commission probing the company’s accounting practices dragged the stock down.

The sharp rebound in NVDA shares on Monday pushed Nvidia’s short value at risk up 150% to $4.68 billion, the highest figure S3 Partners has recorded for any single stock.

Still Ahead For The Year—Barely

Even after Monday’s losses, short sellers remain up about $4 billion on Nvidia for 2026. The stock would need to reach roughly $173 to erase the gains from the seven-day decline and about $182 to wipe out the full year’s profit for the short side, the firm said.

Across Nasdaq names, short sellers had booked $83 billion in gains over the same seven sessions, $36 billion of it on Friday. On Monday, they incurred an estimated $39 billion loss, more than reversing Friday’s profit. Nasdaq shorts are now down about $64 billion for the year, the firm said.

How Did NVDA Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around NVDA stock stayed within the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing, accompanied by ‘extremely high’ retail chatter.

In an ongoing Stocktwits poll, nearly 64% of respondents said that they are more bullish on Nvidia now that Huang is back. 15% said they feel the same as before, while 9% said they are more bearish, and 12% voted that it's too early to tell.

NVDA stock has dropped 12% year-to-date.

data.title: New AI rule marks a first for US federal appeals courts
data.description:
By Nate Raymond

A federal appeals court in Denver has finalized a rule requiring lawyers to certify that any court filings prepared with the assistance of generative AI have been reviewed by humans for accuracy.

  • The 10th US Circuit Court of Appeals is the first federal appeals court to adopt an AI-related rule targeting instances of fake case citations that have shown up in court filings since generative AI debuted on a mass scale in 2022.

  • Litigants are required under the rule to certify that all documents have been reviewed by a human who has independently verified the accuracy and existence of all cited authorities and quotes from court precedent.

  • The rule adopted on Friday applies "regardless of whether the brief, motion or paper was prepared with the assistance of artificial intelligence."

  • The rule allows the court to address violations by deeming the affected issue in a brief as waived; striking non-compliant submissions; dismissing an appeal; imposing monetary sanctions; or referring lawyers for discipline.

  • Chris Wolpert, the 10th Circuit's clerk of court, said the court received only a handful of public comments in response to its September proposal to adopt the rule, which takes effect January 1.

  • The New Orleans-based 5th US Circuit Court of Appeals in 2024 scrapped plans to adopt a similar rule after its proposal drew opposition from members of the bar, who argued existing rules could sufficiently address any issues.

Read more:

US appeals court rule would require lawyers to certify AI-prepared filings

US judiciary developing new guidance on courts' use of AI

5th Circuit scraps plans to adopt AI rule after lawyers object

data.title: Singapore third-quarter GDP grows 6.1%
data.description:
Singapore's economy grew 6.1% in the third quarter of 2026 from a year earlier, government data showed on Tuesday, higher than an official advance estimate of 5.4%.

Economists polled ​by Reuters had expected annual growth ​of 5.6% ​in the third quarter.

On a quarter-on-quarter, seasonally adjusted basis, gross domestic product expanded by 1.5% in the July-September period, compared with an advance estimate of 1.1% growth.

The Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry also upgraded the city-state's growth forecast for 2026 to around 6.0%, up from a range of 4.5% to 5.5%, with 2027 GDP growth expected to come in at a range of 2.5% to 4.5%.

data.title: Nikkei May Rise After Nvidia Led U.S. Stock Gains — Market Talk
data.description:
1841 ET - Japanese stocks may rise after U.S. stocks surged overnight, led by Nvidia. Nikkei futures are up 3.0% at 57840 on the SGX. The dollar is at 158.98 yen, compared with Y159.17 as of Friday's Tokyo stock market close. Japanese markets were closed Monday for a public holiday. Investors are focusing on crude oil prices and bond yields. The Nikkei Stock Average fell 5.1% to 56436.65 on Friday. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com)

1707 ET - The Mexican peso's recent move above 19 to the U.S. dollar for the first time since June 2025 reflects a narrowing gap between the Bank of Mexico's benchmark interest rate and the U.S. federal funds rate, putting pressure on the peso carry trade, Molly Schwartz and Christian Lawrence of Rabobank say in a note. The Bank of Mexico is expected to hold its benchmark rate at 6.25% next month following November's quarter-point cut, while a quarter-point Fed December increase is widely expected. "We expect the [currency] pair to remain near 19 around the December Fed meeting before easing to 18.8 in three months and around 18.5 by mid-2027, as additional Fed hikes priced by markets fail to materialize," they say. The peso is trading around 19.17 to the dollar. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

1644 ET - The Canadian dollar has weakened to its lowest level relative to USD in about two years, or in the early days of elevated U.S.-Canada trade tensions. USDCAD strengthened to C$1.4369 in Monday trading, according to data provider Tullett Prebon. BMO Capital Markets chief economist Douglas Porter says CAD weakness reflects widening US-Canada short term spreads, of nearly 1.5 percentage points based on respective two-year bond yields. "US growth is much firmer — helped much more by the AI buildout and less hampered by trade unceratinty," Porter says, adding US inflation is also stronger. CAD will remain under pressure until the AI trade "truly ebbs," and more certainty emerges on US-Canada trade front, Porter adds. (paul.vieira@wsj.com, @paulvieira)

1420 ET - Fitch Ratings lowers its U.K. water utilities outlook to deteriorating from improving, citing substantial regulatory uncertainty and other factors. "Uncertainty over the new regulatory framework could affect investor confidence, funding costs and long-term investment, if it persists," Fitch says. The uncertainty includes the regulator's independence, powers and tariff-setting approach, Fitch adds. The agency also points out weak operational and environmental performance may persist in fiscal year 2027. Fitch maintains neutral sector outlooks for the U.K. electricity and gas networks for 2027. (stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com)

1344 ET - Fitch Ratings says public finance ratings would be most affected by a potential one-notch downgrade of France's sovereign rating. Fitch revised France's outlook to negative from stable back in October. The agency says it has now tested the sensitivity of its rated portfolio to a potential one-notch French sovereign downgrade to "A." It found that 90% of French public finance ratings would be downgraded. "A sovereign downgrade would lower the sovereign-capped operating-environment score and would be likely to result in downgrades of BNP Paribas, Crédit Agricole and Crédit Mutuel's regional groups." Implications for structured finance, covered bonds and most supranationals would be limited, according to Fitch.(stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com)

1249 ET - With the holidays coming up, many young adults won't have to travel far to get home, Realtor.com says. A record 25.2 million adults ages 18 to 34 lived with their parents in 2025, or 33% of young adults nationwide, according to Realtor.com. The national share remained just below its 2020 peak of 33.6%. The Northeast had the highest share of young adults living with their parents at 36.9% in 2025, even as the region's rate fell to its lowest level since 2010. While most adults ages 18 to 34 living with their parents are ages 18 to 24, adults ages 25 to 34 have grown as a share of the at-home population since the early 2000s. New York had the highest share of young adults living with their parents among the major metros analyzed, at 41.3%. (chris.wack@wsj.com)

1156 ET - Canadian PM Mark Carney's pledge to double housing construction over a decade faces stiff short-term headwinds, according to an analysis from National Bank of Canada. Economist Daren King says there's a wide gap in Canada between construction costs and housing prices. Until that narrows, housing starts are likely to remain depressed in the near term, He says. Since 4Q of 2019 to 3Q this year, the rise in construction expenses, 73.3%, has outstripped the 30% gain in property prices. The cost for materials account for some of the increase, but the big drivers are unit-labor costs. King's research indicates average-weekly earnings in construction rose over 33% in the 2019-2026 period, versus 29% for all Canadian industries. Meanwhile, construction-sector productivity is 18% lower in Canada relative to prepandemic levels. (paul.vieira@wsj.com; @paulvieira)

1106 ET - Mexico's inflation likely edged up in the first half of November, led by increases in energy as residential electricity subsidies ended in additional cities. El Buen Fin, Mexico's Black Friday-style event that ran Nov. 13-17, could keep a lid on core goods prices. The consumer price index is expected to have risen by 0.50% in the first two weeks of the month, pushing the 12-month inflation rate up to 3.92% from 3.88% in the second half of October, according to a WSJ survey of analysts. Core CPI is expected to have risen 0.10%, moving the annual rate to 3.88% from 3.82% in the second half of October. Statistics institute Inegi is scheduled to report mid-November inflation on Tuesday. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

1105 ET - Home-buying demand dropped last quarter, Zillow says. Mortgage rates rose significantly from July through September, leaving fewer serious shoppers competing for each home on the market. The number of engaged home shoppers per listing, signaling real interest beyond casual browsing, fell to 3.5 nationally in 3Q. That is down 4.8% from a year earlier and the lowest level since the second half of 2023. The pullback was widespread, with engagement down from last year in 44 of the 50 largest metro areas, although major Florida markets were an exception. Mortgage rates are still keeping many buyers on the sidelines, and as inventory continues to build, there is less competition for each home for sale. (chris.wack@wsj.com)

1017 ET - Saudi Arabia's willingness to adjust spending on major development projects is helping contain fiscal risks as the kingdom pursues its Vision 2030 economic diversification program, S&P Global Ratings says. Ravi Bhatia, the agency's lead sovereign analyst, says the government and the Public Investment Fund, Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, have shown flexibility in changing the pace of projects to limit pressure on public finances. Although government debt is rising, Saudi Arabia remains in a net asset position, with financial assets exceeding liabilities, he says in S&P's Middle East Credit Gateway video series. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

1016 ET - Saudi Arabia's banking sector alone won't be able to meet the financing needs of the kingdom's large investment projects, S&P Global Ratings says. Speaking on the agency's Middle East Credit Gateway video series, Hina Shoeb, S&P's head of analytics for Saudi Arabia, says banks are exploring alternative funding sources as demand for financing expands. These include private credit, or loans provided by nonbank investors, structured financing and new Islamic financing arrangements that comply with Sharia principles. The development of alternative funding channels could help support investment beyond what traditional bank deposits can finance. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

1009 ET - Saudi Arabia's ability to redirect oil exports through the Red Sea and its growing nonoil economy are helping protect its creditworthiness despite the Middle East conflict, S&P Global Ratings says. Ravi Bhatia, the ratings agency's lead sovereign analyst, says the kingdom's East-West pipeline, which carries crude to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, has helped it avoid some disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz. Higher oil prices have also supported government revenue. Speaking on S&P's Middle East Credit Gateway video series, Bhatia says the agency expects regional tensions to persist into 2027 but remain largely contained. S&P affirmed Saudi Arabia's A+ rating with a stable outlook in September. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

data.title: CFTC staff say exchanges can count Bitcoin toward operating reserves
data.description:
US Commodity Futures Trading Commission staff said Monday that CFTC-regulated derivative exchanges and clearinghouses can count Bitcoin, Ether and payment stablecoins toward meeting their financial resource requirements.

CFTC rules require derivatives exchanges, swap trading venues and clearinghouses to maintain enough financial resources to cover at least 12 months of operating costs on a rolling basis.

The latest staff guidance clarifies that certain crypto assets can count toward part of that requirement, but with a discount to their market value. CFTC staff said they would accept a “haircut” of at least 20% for Bitcoin and Ether and 2% for qualifying payment stablecoins to account for the risk of holding those assets.

The guidance gives CFTC-regulated exchanges and entities more flexibility in how they meet their operating reserve requirements. CFTC-regulated entities include Coinbase Derivatives, Crypto.com’s North American Derivatives Exchange and Bitnomial Exchange, as well as prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket US.

However, they will still need to meet a separate liquidity requirement with assets such as cash or highly liquid securities.

The advisory represents the views of staff at the Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk, and is not considered a formal rule change approved by the Commission.

data.title: CME live cattle futures firm on surprise in USDA cattle report
data.description:
By P.J. Huffstutter

Live cattle futures on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange rose on Monday for a fourth consecutive session, after a monthly government report showed a bigger year-on-year drop in the number of cattle in US feedlots than analysts had expected, traders said.

After the market closed Friday, the USDA reported the number of cattle on feed as of November 1 at 99% of a year ago. Analysts surveyed by Reuters on average had expected a smaller decline, to 99.7%.

"It was a pretty wide miss, and the fourth miss in a row in this report from the market's perspective," said Brodrick Schmidt, a commodity broker and market analyst at U.S. Commodities LLC.

The USDA reported cattle placements into US feedlots during October at 93% of a year ago, below the average analyst estimate of 97%. Marketings during October were 95% of a year ago, near the average analyst estimate of 94.9%.

The report told traders that the US is not rebuilding its cattle herd at a brisk pace, Schmidt said, and "that prices will stay strong as long as consumer demand for beef stays strong."

CME December live cattle settled up 1.550 cents at 224.550 cents per pound, and most-active February futures rose 1.050 cents to 228.750 cents.

January feeder cattle fell 1.100 cents to finish at 334.325 cents per pound on technical trading, market analysts said.

Cash cattle markets have seen steady trade and prices firming, with cattle trades reaching $222 per hundredweight, cwt, last week and prices in the north up $7 per cwt, market analysts said.

The wholesale choice boxed beef cutout value rose $3.35 to $356.19 per hundredweight on Monday morning, the USDA said.

Meanwhile, CME lean hog futures closed mostly lower, pressured by sagging cash hog prices and weak demand for pork.

December lean hog futures (LHZ26) settled 0.150 cent lower at 52.450 cents per pound while most-active February hogs (LHG27) dipped to a fresh contract low during the session, before ending up 0.300 cent at 57.275 cents a pound. Four other lean hog contracts also set fresh lows in Monday's trade.

data.title: Austral Resources Hits High-Grade Copper Intersections at Enterprise Deposit
data.description:
Austral Resources Australia has intersected high-grade copper at its Enterprise deposit in Queensland, with initial results supporting further drilling to test extensions beyond the existing resource.

The standout intersection returned 14 metres at 3.00% copper from 118m downhole, including 11m at 3.70%, in the first batch of assays from the 2026 program.

Another hole encountered several zones of copper mineralisation at greater depth, while separate drilling confirmed copper from surface.

The results come from the first six holes of a program intended to improve confidence in the existing deposit and investigate opportunities for resource growth.

High Grades in Multiple Zones

The strongest result contained bornite and chalcocite, which Austral interprets as evidence of localised enrichment along a geological contact that helped channel copper-bearing fluids.

In another hole, drilling intersected 27m at 1.21% copper from 151m, followed by 17m at 1.37% from 197m and 13m at 1.73% from 228m.

Those deeper intersections contain primary copper sulphides rather than the secondary enrichment seen in the standout result, supporting Austral’s interpretation of a higher-grade trend extending downwards.

Near-surface drilling separately returned 28m at 0.61% copper from surface, including 7m at 0.96%, providing additional information for evaluating shallow mineralisation.

The reported intervals are downhole lengths, with true widths estimated at around 60% of those lengths and subject to local variation.

Existing MRE and Untested Strike

Enterprise has an existing inferred mineral resource estimate of 0.95 million tonnes at 0.97% copper using a 0.5% copper cut-off grade.

That estimate reflects historical drilling on sections approximately 120–125m apart across almost 800m of strike, leaving scope for closer-spaced drilling to clarify grade continuity.

Surface copper anomalies extend over approximately two kilometres, considerably beyond the strike covered by the historical resource drilling.

The deposit remains open down dip and down plunge, although the extent and continuity of any additional mineralisation have yet to be established.

Austral is also reviewing historical density assumptions, with further measurements and modelling required before any change to resource tonnage can be assessed.

Resource Growth Drilling

A further 17 percussion holes are planned to examine higher-grade extensions, potential fault-displaced mineralisation northwest of the resource and continuity within the known deposit.

Preliminary metallurgical test work on near-surface oxide and transitional copper mineralisation is being prepared to assess its potential processing characteristics.

New drilling results, geological interpretations, and density measurements are intended to feed into a subsequent update of the Enterprise resource model.

"Enterprise is the latest in a strong run of results from our exploration team this year [that] points to real upside ,not only at Enterprise but across AR's broader tenure, which anchors our organic growth strategy,” chair David Newling said.

“Taken together, Snow Queen, McLeod Hill, Canyon, Waterhole, and now Enterprise show a clear development pathway for the company as it works towards becoming Australia's next mid-tier copper powerhouse."

data.title: CFTC finalises permanent data-reporting rules for event contracts
data.description:
The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission finalized permanent data-reporting rules for certain event contracts on Monday, aiming to strengthen oversight of prediction markets.

  • The rule comes as prediction markets face growing regulatory scrutiny in the US, with questions over federal oversight and market integrity

  • The final rule creates an alternative reporting framework for certain fully collateralised event contracts that have operated under CFTC staff no-action relief since 2017

  • "The CFTC will no longer regulate market participants through a patchwork of no-action letters, which serve as band-aids for unworkable regulations. This final rule is an important step in future-proofing the regulatory framework for event contracts," Chairman Michael Selig said

  • Under the new framework, reporting markets, futures commission merchants, clearing members and foreign brokers will report data under Parts 15-18 of CFTC regulations, instead of relying on reporting provisions spread across Parts 38, 39, 43 and 45

  • The move follows other efforts by the regulator to strengthen federal oversight of prediction markets, including an earlier proposal to classify certain event contracts as swaps

data.title: Asian Currencies Consolidate But May Strengthen Amid Risk-on Sentiment — Market Talk
data.description: Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar in early trade, but may strengthen amid risk-on sentiment driven by Wall Street's rally overnight. "Risk appetite returned with a vengeance after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, triggering a sharp rebound across battered AI and technology stocks," StoneX's Matt Simpson says in commentary. Although worries over artificial-intelligence valuations, elevated interest rates and slowing economic growth haven't disappeared, there's an improved risk environment, the senior market analyst adds. The U.S. dollar is flat at 1,340.96 won and is little changed at 1.2913 Singapore dollars, while the Australian dollar is steady at US$0.6624, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
